committee_name.text: Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC)

quote.quote: This BLA was discussed with the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on 10 June 2015.
This BLA was discussed with the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on 10 June 2015.

recommendation.text: On the key voting question of whether the LDL-C-lowering benefit of evolocumab exceeds its risks to support approval in one or more populations excluding HoFH, 11 members voted yes and 4 voted no; yes-voters unanimously supported approval for HeFH, while several agreed evolocumab should not be approved as monotherapy or for low/moderate CV risk or mixed dyslipidemia. For HoFH, the committee voted unanimously for approval.

quote.quote: Eleven members voted "yes" and four members voted "no." In their comments, members who voted "yes" unanimously supported approval for HeFH.

linkages.concern: The committee advised that benefit/risk did not support the applicant's broad proposed indication: members supported HeFH but several agreed evolocumab should not be approved as monotherapy or for low/moderate CV risk or mixed dyslipidemia, given the limited safety database and residual uncertainty about LDL-C as a surrogate.
linkages.change: The indication for primary hyperlipidemia/mixed dyslipidemia was narrowed; the approved indication was limited to adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease who require additional LDL-C lowering, as an adjunct to maximally tolerated statin therapy (no monotherapy or broad primary-hyperlipidemia indication).

concern_quote.quote: Several members agreed that evolocumab should not be approved as monotherapy or for patient populations such as low or moderate CV risk or mixed dyslipidemia.

change_quote.quote: Following the advice we obtained from the EMDAC, the review team discussed the proposed indication at length. We proposed, and the applicant ultimately accepted, modifying the indication for primary hyperlipidemia/mixed dyslipidemia to "REPATHA is indicated as an adjunct to diet and maximally tolerated statin therapy for the treatment of adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, who require additional lowering of LDL-C."

linkages.concern: The committee judged the safety database inadequate for widespread use, noting it was limited in both number of patients and duration of exposure and that many studies did not enroll the high-CV-risk target population, leaving long-term safety uncertain.
linkages.change: Approval was limited to patients at very high cardiovascular risk pending completion of a cardiovascular outcomes trial, with the long-term safety concerns to be studied as post-marketing requirements.

concern_quote.quote: the safety database was not adequate to comfortably state that there was no reason for concern with widespread use

change_quote.quote: This uncertainty regarding long-term safety contributed to the recommendation of Dr. Craig and the advisory committee members to limit approval to patients at very high cardiovascular risk, where the benefit/risk is expected to be more favorable, until we can better quantitate clinical benefit and longer-term risk through the completion of a CVOT. Risks of concern will be studied as post-marketing requirements (see below).

linkages.concern: For the HoFH 420 mg Q2W dosing regimen proposed as an alternative, the committee generally agreed there was insufficient evidence that it provides benefit beyond the 420 mg QM (once-monthly) regimen.
linkages.change: The 420 mg Q2W regimen was not approved; the review team concluded the limited safety and efficacy data for the every-2-week dose were insufficient to support approval at that time.

concern_quote.quote: the committee generally agreed that there is insufficient evidence that this regimen provides benefit beyond 420 mg QM

change_quote.quote: the limited amount of safety and efficacy data provided in this submission for the 420 mg every 2 week dose is insufficient to support approval at this time, especially as this dosing regimen could be used in children

summary: Repatha (evolocumab, BLA125522) was reviewed by the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on 10 June 2015. The committee voted 11-4 that benefit/risk supported approval in at least one non-HoFH population and voted unanimously for approval in HoFH, but members flagged a limited safety database and residual uncertainty about LDL-C as a surrogate. Following EMDAC's advice, FDA narrowed the broad proposed indication to adults with HeFH or clinical ASCVD on maximally tolerated statins, limited approval to very-high-risk patients pending a cardiovascular outcomes trial with safety concerns deferred to post-marketing requirements, and did not approve the 420 mg every-2-week regimen.
